headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: AutoGen’s code-executing orchestration can feed Dexter’s autonomous, API-heavy workflow with sensitive outputs by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and execute tool calls; Dexter uses autonomous execution and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. If Dexter content is copied into AutoGen prompts or files, instruction-like text can be treated as trusted. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Dexter scratchpad content is ingested by AutoGen as prompt text or file input
IF the two agents share a writable workspace or manual copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Strip instructions from shared files before ingestion
Use a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and broad filesystem access, while Dexter touches financial and market data and calls multiple external APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or third-party calls. The profiles do not prove a shared OS workspace, so medium is the safest supported choice.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same filesystem workspace
IF either agent is given the other’s files or secrets
IF Dexter forwards shared context to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Keep API keys in distinct secret stores
Mount read-only inputs for one-way transfer
Redact financial data before sharing outputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; Dexter also performs autonomous execution and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared local state if co-located, creating write conflicts and race conditions. Because shared locking is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF either agent writes artifacts the other later edits
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
Make shared files read-only
Use file locks for mutable artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Dexter runs autonomously with broad API access. If Dexter consumes AutoGen’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into external API calls or financial-research actions. Because the downstream blast radius can extend beyond a single document and no default verification is shown, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Dexter uses AutoGen output as a direct input to autonomous actions
IF no verification or human approval step exists between agents
IF AutoGen outputs factual claims that Dexter operationalizes
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require citations for any factual claims passed onward
Limit Dexter to draft-only mode
Log and review cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add policy gates before external API actions

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while AutoGen handles application data and model-provider secrets. If financial data is routed through AutoGen’s broader execution environment or logs, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdiction or certifications, so this is a compliance-risk medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through AutoGen logs or prompts
IF the two agents have different retention or deletion policies
IF either agent stores data outside the operator’s compliance boundary
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data across the pair
Review retention settings for both agents
Disable or minimize logging of sensitive prompts
Keep compliance-sensitive workloads in one agent only
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
